Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
841 PM EDT Fri Oct 23 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No major changes were made to the previous forecast. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Frost or freezing temperatures are possible in many areas
  tonight, Saturday night, and Sunday night.

- 2) Dry weather continues through next week along with 
  generally seasonable temperatures.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Frost or freezing temperatures are possible in
many areas tonight, Saturday night, and Sunday night.

With a large area of Canadian high pressure building overhead
through the weekend, conditions will likely become favorable 
for radiational cooling (light to calm winds, mainly clear skies
and a cool background airmass). At the moment it is unclear
which night will be the coldest, although Saturday night will
have a slight advantage given the position of the high.

The growing season for 2026 has ended along and west of the Blue
Ridge and Catoctin Mountains, but continues east of there. Any
headlines for frost/freeze conditions will only be issued where
the growing season remains active.

For tonight, temperatures look to fall into the mid to upper 30s
for many areas (slightly colder west of the Blue Ridge and
slightly warmer in the urban areas and bayshore). The typically
colder spots of northern MD and the central VA piedmont could 
at least briefly come close to freezing. For the afternoon 
package, a Frost Advisory was only issued from Frederick to 
Cecil Counties. These areas will be closer to the surface high 
and have lower surface dew points. Farther to the south, there 
will be a background easterly flow and perhaps some residual 
clouds.

For Saturday night, more widespread cold (possible frost/freeze)
conditions are possible as high pressure settles more directly 
overhead. This would bring the frost/freeze threat for most 
areas outside the major urban centers and immediate shore of the
Chesapeake Bay. If the colder temperature guidance verifies, 
then the growing season may end for more areas west I-95 come 
early Sunday morning. The high will remain overhead through 
Monday morning, and the low level airmass doesn't change 
appreciably, so frost/freeze conditions will be possible again 
Sunday night.

Did not make appreciable changes to the previous min temperature
forecasts, which are near or below the coldest guidance which 
performs best in radiational cooling (MOS, NBM 10 percentile and
Canadian Regional).


KEY MESSAGE 2...Dry weather continues through next week along
with generally seasonable temperatures.

Canadian high pressure will continue to prevail overhead over the 
next several days as upper-level ridging builds in from the west. As 
this ridging tracks east, a dry backdoor cold front will move 
through Tuesday and into Wednesday, with winds shifting 
northeasterly in the wake of the front. With PWATs remaining dry 
through this period, no precipitation is anticipated as this front 
moves through. 

As this surface high pressure continues on, temperatures remain 
seasonable, with highs in the 60s to low-70s. Overnight lows could
gradually increase somewhat throughout the week as this high 
pressure persists, with skies remaining mostly clear throughout the 
week. A few models hint at this high pressure breaking down towards 
the end of next week as a weak trough begins to form over the Ohio 
River Valley next Thursday. Regardless, expect continued dry & 
seasonable conditions to continue at least through the next several 
days as the current pattern remains largely unchanged.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
VFR conditions are expected to prevail through early next week.
There are some hints that a slight uptick in low-level moisture
could lead to some patchy fog during the early morning hours
through the weekend, though confidence in timing and extent of 
sub-VFR is low at this time.

Light E to NE winds this afternoon will become light to calm 
tonight. A more E to SE flow is likely Saturday, with light to 
calm winds again Saturday night. Wind direction may be a bit 
variable, ranging from SE to NE as high pressure passes directly
overhead Sunday. 

VFR conditions are anticipated to continue across terminals 
through Wednesday as conditions remain dry across the Mid-
Atlantic. Light westerly winds Monday shift northerly on 
Tuesday, then east to southeasterly on Wednesday in the wake of 
a backdoor cold front.

&&

.MARINE...
E to SE winds are expected tonight into Saturday. SCAs continue
through 2 AM across the lower Potomac to Tangier Sound. While 
winds may increase elsewhere, advisory level gusts look to be 
brief in duration if they occur.

High pressure will build overhead this weekend. Winds will vary
a bit from northeast to southeast, but at light speeds less than
10 knots. Winds stay below SCA criteria Monday. A dry backdoor
cold front passing through could briefly bring wind gusts near
SCA criteria on Tuesday before diminishing again overnight. 
Westerly winds shift northerly Tuesday, then easterly Wednesday 
in the wake of the front.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Generally light but steady northeast to east winds are expected
to keep water levels elevated through the upcoming weekend. 
When paired with high astronomical tides due to the upcoming 
full moon on October 26, additional rounds of minor tidal 
flooding are possible. There has been a slight trend downward,
so there is some decrease in confidence for which locations 
reach minor flooding in forthcoming high tides. Guidance does 
show a more notable decline in water levels by Monday when flow 
finally turns westerly.
